extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, institutional PIs and grant applicants preparing NIAID/NIH G11 or similar grant applications (especially LMIC institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: A complete sample SF424 (R&R) + PHS application illustrating required fields, organization, facilities/resources, personnel biosketches, human/animal subject reporting, monitoring & evaluation, and a staff training plan for an NIAID G11 award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application-format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted use of sample text
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the application is copyrighted. The awardee provided express permission for NIAID to post this grant application and summary statement for educational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use material (data, writing, graphics) shared in the applications for nonprofit educational purposes only, provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigators, awardee organizations, and NIH NIAID are credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA/confidentiality expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH responds to FOIA requests for grant applications and summary statements, the material will be subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH must protect all confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance / accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility: the sample was reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have trouble accessing content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF424 (R&R) cover and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: SF424 R&R application must include required cover fields (type of submission, federal identifier, dates, applicant information, EIN/TIN, type of applicant, type of application, name of federal agency, CFDA number/title, descriptive project title, proposed start/end dates, congressional districts, contact PD/PI info, estimated funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness of checkboxes and fields (e.g., Are Human Subjects Involved? Are Vertebrate Animals Used?), provide contact person, authorized representative signature, and track submission identifiers (Grants.gov tracking, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant certifications and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the authorized representative certifies to the statements contained in the list of certifications and provides required assurances and agrees to comply with any resulting terms if an award is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of legal liability for false statements (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). The list of certifications and assurances or a site where they can be obtained is contained in the announcement or agency-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project/performance site information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide primary project/performance site location(s), organization name(s), full address(es), and congressional district(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting as an individual, indicate; otherwise provide organizational DUNS and site details. Include additional locations as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Other Project Information elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Research & Related Other Project Information section, answering whether human subjects are involved, vertebrate animals used, whether proprietary information is included, environmental impacts, historic place designation, and international activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects/animals are involved, provide exemption status, IRB/IACUC review status and approval dates, assurance numbers, and explanations where required. Provide project summary/abstract, project narrative, bibliography & references, facilities & other resources, and equipment attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Project Summary/Abstract (attachment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a concise summary that describes the project aims and significance (file: Project_Summary.pdf in sample).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Project Narrative (attachment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Narrative provides a short public-health-relevance statement for non-scientific audiences (file: Project_Narrative.pdf in sample).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional environment and resources that will contribute to project success (training facilities, intellectual resources, office space, computers, IT, administrative support, library resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how facilities and environment enable successful implementation (e.g., rooms, videoconferencing, internet access, libraries, institutional networks). For partner institutions, list relevant systems and offices that support training and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment – contribution to success
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the institution's environment (experience with funding, research portfolio, organizational structure) will contribute to success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details such as history of NIH funding, administrative units supporting grants, staff numbers and roles, and examples of relevant intellectual resources and experienced faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of institutional resources & systems (partner-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: For partner institutions, list grants management systems, policies, SOPs, templates, and technology platforms that will be used for training and benchmarking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example systems: Cayuse 424, GW Documents, Enterprise Accounting System, GW TeamSites, Huron Research Suite. Indicate how interacting with these systems will build capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketches for senior/key personnel (format & length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biographical sketches for senior/key personnel following the specified format; DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, eRA Commons username, position title, education/training (institution, degree, dates, field), personal statement, and attach Current & Pending Support. Follow the required structure for each person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan / Table of Contents organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the application with the recommended Table of Contents order: SF424 R&R Cover Page; Table of Contents; Performance Sites; Research & Related Other Project Information; Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Facilities & Other Resources; Research & Related Senior/Key Person; Budget sections; PHS Research Plan (Specific Aims, Research Strategy); PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information; Bibliography & References Cited; Letters of Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the TOC to ensure all required components are present and in standard sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy components (Specific Aims, Research Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Specific Aims and Research Strategy sections in the PHS Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this sample is a G11 capacity-building application rather than a hypothesis-driven research study, include aims and a research strategy appropriate to the FOA (e.g., training aims, implementation of systems). For typical NIH R-series, address Significance, Innovation, and Approach as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects reporting and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer whether human subjects are involved; if yes, indicate exemption status, applicable exemption number, IRB review pending/approved, IRB approval date, and Human Subject Assurance Number. Provide explanation for use of human specimens/data not considered human subjects research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information form with required justifications and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If vertebrate animals are used, answer Yes and provide IACUC review pending/approval status, IACUC approval date, and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply required justifications and documentation in the animals section of Research & Related Other Project Information and the PHS forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Monitoring & Evaluation framework elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an M&E framework that identifies expected results, indicators (what), means of verification, timing/frequency, and targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample includes a table with Outputs, Indicators, Means of Verification, WHEN (frequency: e.g., at 9 months, 18 months), and explicit numeric targets. Use measurable indicators and defined verification sources (training reports, attendance logs, platform statistics, project reports, case studies, FAQs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify measurable performance targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Define numeric targets and timepoints for outputs and outcomes (e.g., percentage of senior administrators trained, number of junior administrators mentored, number of SOPs reviewed/updated, number of trainings and webinars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample sets targets (e.g., 2 senior administrators trained, 69 junior administrators mentored, 25 regional administrators trained, review 2 SOPs per month, develop 1 SOP per month in 5 months, create a grants tracking system). Use concrete numbers and schedule (e.g., 9- and 18-month targets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training plan specifics and delivery modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the training plan content, modes, frequency and locations (hands-on training at partner institution, attendance at GMP/NIAID workshops, webinars, weekly sessions, regional workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample details: one hands-on training per year for 2 years for 2 senior admins; attendance to GMP training and NIAID regional workshop; one session per week for 4 weeks for each admin category; two webinars per month for 3 months; four 4-day workshops for research scientists. Specify cascade plans for trained staff to mentor juniors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff mentorship and knowledge-sharing mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Include structured mentorship and peer-support mechanisms (e.g., Research Administrator Buddy Program, online Learning Café, online suggestion box) to cascade training and provide ongoing support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define enrollment and engagement targets (e.g., percentage enrolled in RA-Buddy, number of administrators actively engaged on online Café), monitoring methods (platform statistics, monthly reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: SOP and systems development metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and document review, update and development of SOPs and implementation of grants management systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify rates (e.g., review 2 SOPs per month for 5 months, develop 1 SOP per month for 5 months), expected number of SOPs updated/developed (e.g., at least 10 updated, 5 developed), and development/monitoring of a Grants Tracking System with monthly performance review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide letters of institutional support and demonstrate integration of project activities into institutional grants management and training strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document management commitments (time, facilities, access to training rooms, libraries, administrative services), and state how the project will be sustained or integrated (e.g., inclusion in college newsletter, seminar series, institutional staffing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments and filenames for required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach required documents and name files appropriately (Project_Summary.pdf, Project_Narrative.pdf, Bibliography_and_references.pdf, Facilities_and_Resources.pdf, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all referenced attachments are included and match the forms' required contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard forms and identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the prescribed forms and include identifiers such as Grants.gov tracking numbers, Funding Opportunity Number (FOA), Competition ID, Accession Number, IPF, and Council/Competition details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate form metadata fields correctly (FOA title, FOA number, Clinical Trial allowed/not allowed, new/investigator flags) and provide proper role categories for personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key personnel roles and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: List senior/key personnel with organization, role category (PD/PI, co-investigator, consultant, member of advisory committee), attach biosketches and current & pending support documents for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe responsibilities and institutional affiliation; for consultants include specifying role (e.g., Consultant GWU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify monitoring and reporting cadence for project performance (e.g., monthly review of performance, quarterly PAC meetings, M&E at 9 and 18 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify sources for verification (training reports, project reports, individual time sheets, questionnaires) and how feedback will be used (platform statistics, online suggestion box).
